headline: Chip Rout Meets Retail Rally as Market Splits Under the Surface
body_html:
The market is divided at midday on Friday. Of the 663 stocks we track, 346 are higher and 311 are lower, so the overall picture looks calm. Underneath, money is moving sharply from one corner of the market to another. These are intraday readings, and prices are not final.

Semiconductors are the main drag, down 4.44% as a group. Applied Optoelectronics is off 9.81%, Silicon Motion is down 9.28%, MaxLinear has lost 9.08% and Sandisk is down 8.64%. Energy is also weak, down 1.10%. Homebuilders lead the other way, up 1.96%, followed by consumer shares at 1.25% and financials at 0.45%. Gap is the standout mover, up 12.89%, with The Buckle gaining 8.80% alongside it.

Into the close, the questions are whether the chip selling spreads or steadies, and whether buyers keep hold of the apparel names. Traders will also watch Washington, where a possible government shutdown looms, and trade and Taiwan tensions that remain unresolved. The next trading day is Monday, November 23.

briefs.headline: Apparel Names Surge at the Front of the Pack
briefs.body: Gap is up 12.89% and The Buckle has gained 8.80%, making them the two strongest movers in our universe. Floor & Decor is up 3.55% as well. Retail and consumer shares are rising together, and the consumer group is up 1.25% on the session.

briefs.headline: Chip Complex Takes the Heaviest Losses
briefs.body: Semiconductors are down 4.44% as a group, the weakest sector we track by a wide margin. Optical components, storage controllers and memory names all fall roughly 9%. Ichor Holdings, a chip-equipment supplier, is down 8.18%, so the weakness reaches beyond chipmakers.

briefs.headline: Energy Slips as Oil Heads for Third Weekly Loss
briefs.body: The energy group is down 1.10%, while crude is on course for a third straight weekly decline. Reports point to strong export flows from the Middle East. Fuel-cell maker Bloom Energy is down 8.73%, one of the session's sharper drops.

briefs.headline: Anthropic's Record Offering Lands Despite Choppy Tape
briefs.body: Anthropic has completed a record public offering, and underwriters have exercised their overallotment option. The deal went ahead even as one account called the market backdrop massively disruptive. Investors will want to see how the new shares trade.

briefs.headline: Shutdown Worries Build in Washington
briefs.body: Congress is struggling to avoid a government shutdown, with the war involving Iran dividing lawmakers. Funding fights tend to add to nervousness late in the week. Traders heading into the weekend may be reluctant to hold large positions.

briefs.headline: U.S.-China Frictions Linger After Asia Trip
briefs.body: Trade, Taiwan and technology disputes between Washington and Beijing remain unresolved as President Trump returns from Asia. That matters for chip shares, which are already under pressure today. Any update before the close could move the group further.
